description: Manage an existing document’s CLM record: set creates/patches terms or links a signed amendment; renew starts the next term; terminate closes tracking. Requires a tracking plan. Read first: include terms.updated_at for existing terms or links; renew requires the current term and updated_at, terminate requires updated_at. A conflict needs a fresh read and user review, never blind retries. Only supplied terms change; external_references replaces the list; null can clear values or unlink a pending amendment. Assinafy owns auto-renewal and owner reminders; changes can trigger lifecycle emails/webhooks. These actions do not sign, send or cancel the document itself. Use only for changes the user authorized.

terms.description: Every attribute is optional and only the ones sent change. `null` clears an attribute, except `auto_renew` (back to `false`) and `currency` (back to `BRL` while a `value` is set); `status` does not accept `null`. A changed `end_date` starts a new `term`.

auto_renew.description: Whether the hourly run starts the next term the day after `end_date`, by `renewal_term_months`, instead of expiring the contract.

counterparty_name.description: Emoji are kept; other characters outside the 3-byte range are dropped.

counterparty_taxpayer_id.description: A valid CPF or CNPJ, formatted or not.

currency.description: Three letters, such as `BRL` or `USD`, stored in capitals; `BRL` when a `value` is set without one.

external_references.description: Replaces the whole list; `[]` or `null` clears it. Two items whose `system` and `id` compare equal case aside are one reference (the first sent is kept); a pair the database takes for one beyond that (accents, `ß` and `ss`) answers `400`.

id.description: Kept as sent; must not contain emoji or other 4-byte characters.

system.description: Letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`; stored in lower case.

metadata.description: Your own fields: up to 50 keys of 1 to 40 letters, digits, `_`, `-` or `.`, each holding plain text of at most 500 characters; no number under a key ending in `_at`, or `stuck_since`.

notice_period_days.description: Days before `end_date` the notice period starts (`document_contract_renewal_notice`); none when unset.

owner_id.description: An active member of this workspace.

parent_document_id.description: Links the document as an amendment of this contract document, or of any document in its family (resolved to the root); `null` unlinks a pending amendment. With it, the other attributes are the terms the instrument changes, not terms of its own; on a pending amendment a `null` value drops that term from the delta rather than clearing it on the parent.

relation_type.description: Required on the first link. `amendment` may change `value`, `currency`, `start_date` (effective from, display only), `end_date`, `auto_renew`, `renewal_term_months`, `notice_period_days`, `counterparty_name`, `counterparty_taxpayer_id` and `metadata`; `renewal` only `end_date` and `value`; `termination` only `end_date` (the effective date).

renewal_term_months.description: How far a renewal by the term moves `end_date`; 12 when unset.

status.description: On creation any status, so a contract that ended before it was tracked is registered as it ended: `expired` needs an `end_date` in the past, `terminated` its `end_date`; neither is walked by the lifecycle. Afterwards only `draft` or `active` (a contract in force never goes back to `draft`): `expired` and `terminated` are set by the lifecycle and the terminate endpoint; a closed contract is reopened by renewing it.

updated_at.description: Optional precondition: the `updated_at` the client read the contract (or this document's amendment link) with, as the API returned it. If the contract or link changed since, nothing is written and the answer is `409` with `code: ContractChanged`. Not sent, or `null`: the write applies whatever changed meanwhile (last write wins). Compared to the second; a fraction of a second, as a JavaScript date prints it, is read and ignored. New terms and a first link have nothing to have read, so sending one answers `409`; on a pending amendment, send the link's own `updated_at` (the GET on that document).

end_date.description: The new end date, after the current one. Absent, empty or `null`: the current end date plus the renewal term, stepped until it is in the future; `term` is then required.

term.description: The term this renewal starts from, the contract's current `term`. Required unless `end_date` is sent; for a contract in another term the renewal is refused, so a repeated request never renews twice.

updated_at.description: Optional precondition: the contract's `updated_at` as read. Changed since: `409`, nothing renewed.

value.description: The new value; unchanged when not sent, cleared by `null`.

reason.description: Kept in the `document_contract_terminated` event; HTML is stripped.
